title: 2026 UK CBAM actual-emissions verification-record QA controls

sources.title: Keeping records for Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)

facts.source_fact: Importers choosing actual emissions must keep evidence that reported emissions data has been verified.
The evidence may be a supplier-provided verification report or verification summary.
The verification evidence must contain the relevant emissions data.
The report or summary relevant to emission intensity on the tax return must be retained for six years.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve retention period and return linkage.

facts.source_fact: HMRC plans further verification detail before 1 January 2027.
A default emissions value must be used if actual emissions data is unavailable.
A default emissions value must also be used if verification evidence is unavailable.
facts.expected_handling: Do not accept unverified actual data.

facts.source_fact: Default emissions values were still to be set later in 2026 in the guidance reviewed.
Actual-emissions verification evidence is separate from goods/import records.
Verified actual data is preferred but not mandatory where the default-value route is used lawfully.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat actual-data absence as automatic noncompliance.
